title: A proved duration bound excludes one 19-year G2874 transit in the tested companion-cloud model
abstract: We prove a global upper bound on a single eclipse by a cloud whose fixed radius is a fraction of the pericenter Hill radius. The proof includes a finite star, a necessary depth-area condition, and every eccentricity, orientation and inclination. For G2874 at an assumed apocenter of 11.91 au, a 0.95-solar-mass primary and a full Hill cloud, the bound is 11.110 years for 13 Jupiter masses and 14.961 years for 80 Jupiter masses. A generous stellar case gives 16.731 years. A separate uniform-radius bound stays below 17 years for all apocenters up to 11.91 au in the tested discrete mass and stellar cases. Thus one continuous 19-year eclipse is excluded in this support model without relying on a numerical optimizer. The bound is loose and does not prove a circular orbit is optimal. Sparse plates do not establish continuous obscuration, and the infrared models do not measure an upper companion distance. We supply the proof, original code, numerical checks, model tables and source hashes.

display.caption: Proved time bounds and circular contact times at fixed apocenter under the stated stellar and cloud assumptions.

citations.reason: Reported historical duration and depth motivate the test.
